title: Recorder
summary: An alto recorder built from the published measurements of one real baroque alto (a Bressan recorder of the Frans Brueggen collection, as tabulated by Jan Bouterse): the bore of its three joints, the thumb hole and six finger holes, the window, the labium and step, and the windway length; then every length is scaled by 0.9067 to sound at A = 440 on average. The six note pages play it with every length scaled by 0.9067, to sound at A = 440 on average (brought to pitch; the flatness the scale corrects is not explained). The windway height is not published for this instrument and is estimated from other altos. Four fingerings of the first register, F4, A4, Bb4 and B4 from Bouterse's table, are rendered as slow crescendos that choose no pressure at all, and F4 and A4 also as held notes at a pressure read from published register-jump thresholds. The scale and melody add G4, C5, D5, E5 and F5 from the American Recorder Society's alto chart, which names no recorder. C5 to F5 are blown at one player's measured pressures from Blanc's 2009 thesis, on a Zen-On Bressan alto with a machined aluminium chamfered head, not the maker's own; Blanc reports the makers Henri Gohin and Philippe Bolton judging the channel of those machined heads too low. Speaks; not graded on the site. It speaks, but it does not sound like a recorder yet: on the crescendos its first register holds from 78 to 103 Pa up to 444 and 480 Pa on F4 and A4, and to the top of the ramp on Bb4 and B4, where a real Bressan alto has already jumped to its second register (at 230, 305, 505 and 490 Pa); under its first register it sounds higher modes of the pipe. Listening only: screened recordings of recorders exist in the library (84 valid clips on 18 pitches from Bb4 to E6, from several instruments, sources and licences, none of this Bressan alto), but the grader's library is built from UIowa-named files and holds none of them, so no pair is graded and nothing here claims to match a real recorder.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing pressure through the viscous windway law with the published windway length, the published window length as the jet length and the window width as the flue width, acting on a connected duct network (one jet drives the whole graph)

the published bore of the head, middle joint and foot as equal-volume cylinders (the head's oval at its area-equivalent diameter), the thumb hole and six finger holes as chimney sections on ideal junctions (chimney height from the published outer diameter and the local bore), open or closed per the published fingerings, each open hole with its inner length (the Dubos-Dalmont law at its local bore), its matching length and its series length (Garcia Mayen et al. 2021, eqs. 12 and 10; the series length is taken off the bore on each side of the hole), and the bore closed by the block behind the window

the window as an acoustic mass from Ernoult and Fabre 2017's closed form (fitted to 444 finite-element windows) for the published 12.0 x 4.6 mm cut with parallel cheeks and the labium ramp, moved from their edge plane to the window centre, in place of a textbook end correction; the 3-D potential-flow solve of the same cut still runs as the comparison; the network keeps the window's channel only as a one-sample inlet line, so no 1-D line rings across a channel whose cross modes start at 13.5 kHz
hole 7 on the foot at a derived position (24 mm below the socket rim, bracket 18 to 30 mm), open in a1, b-flat1 and b1 as the published fingerings open it

breath as the gas in the bore: exhaled breath saturated with water at 27 C with its published 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 (dry), the woodwind breath law, read from the shared woodwind breath gas pack; it lowers every passive mode 19.1 to 19.3 cents below saturated air

fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the long bore sections (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops its memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, adbb97dbb and f78078db2)

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops the open holes and the foot's open end take the compact unflanged-pipe load instead, Garcia Mayen 2021, Eq. 14, with Silva et al. 2009, Eqs. 10-11, the foot's from ae3ef2d4e, and are still heard as baffled sources), plus the window, which radiates from the outer face of the same 3-D solve on the head's rigid outer cylinder (resistance from the cylindrical-harmonic series, its static mass by Kramers-Kronig and taken out of the window mass, a passive chain of parallel R-L-C cells fitted from 20 Hz to 24 kHz within 1.9 %) in place of an authored window loss (on the six note pages and the scale and melody stops that radiation's memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, 27631e7a4)
deterministic oscillation: every held note sounds the same pitch and level for another jet seed, so it is a limit cycle and not a filtered seed

the first register's pitch on the crescendos the site serves. Those pages play this alto with every length scaled by 0.9067, a factor chosen to bring the pages to A = 440 on average (brought to pitch; the flatness it corrects is not explained), so the cents here are of equal temperament on A = 440. In its first-register span (the 100 ms windows in the first 1.5 s, below 153 Pa, whose strongest line from 150 to 2500 Hz is within 100 cents of the passive first mode and whose level is within 40 dB of the clip's loudest 100 ms) the crescendos sound F4 -3.9, A4 -40.9, B-flat4 -13.9 and B4 -25.3 cents (medians of 6, 5, 7 and 5 windows; the pitch climbs with the pressure, -11.3 to +1.0 on F4, -51.2 to -37.2 on A4, -40.2 to -6.3 on B-flat4, -35.2 to -20.4 on B4), where the passive first modes of the served cards are -3.0, -30.0, +5.9 and -5.7 cents (a transfer-matrix port of each card with the terms its render realised: the open holes' inner, matching and series lengths, the unflanged open end and holes, the window's computed mass and its radiation on the head's outer cylinder, the bore gas at 27 C). Below 153 Pa the jet holds the first register 0.9, 10.9, 19.8 and 19.6 cents under the passive modes. That 27 C is the shared woodwind breath gas: the mean bore gas of a played mouth-blown woodwind, after Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969 and Fletcher and Rossing. A played Baroque flute measured with thermocouples along its bore averaged 27.3 C in a 20.6 C room (Soubeyran, Padfield, Gohin and Spohr). Bouterse's pitches for this alto were played in a 15 C room: f1 -14.8, a1 -34.8, b-flat1 -4.8 and b1 +5.2 cents of equal temperament on a1 = 409 Hz. A uniform scale and a uniform bore temperature move every note alike, so only the intervals compare with the served pages: from F4, the crescendos give A4 -37.0, B-flat4 -10.0, B4 -21.4 cents, against Bouterse's -20.0, +10.0, +20.0: narrower by 17.0, 20.0 and 41.4 cents. Nothing is added to close it

breath noise at the flue: the `jet_noise` row (seed 14), a pressure source at the flue jet of rms 0.0013 of the jet's rho U^2 / 2 inside the Strouhal band St_h 0.045 to 0.115, open while the flue's Re_h = U h / nu is at least 700, which this flue (h 0.96 mm, the card's air) reaches at 72 Pa. Every page clears it: F4 held at 135 Pa (Re_h 959), A4 held at 210 Pa (Re_h 1196), and the four crescendos from 0.69 s, reaching 2021 at their 600 Pa peak. The constant, band and gate come from Verge's measurement of a flue jet at a labium with a 1 mm slit (PhD thesis, TU Eindhoven 1995, sec. 5.5), not determinable below Re_h about 1700, which this flue reaches at 424 Pa: the held pages and the crescendos' first 4.24 s take that gain below its measured range. The binary has no noise tap, so the noise's own level in the clip is not read apart
physics_missing: a graded comparison: screened recordings of recorders exist in the library (84 valid clips on 18 pitches from Bb4 to E6, from several instruments, sources and licences, none of this Bressan alto), but the grader's library is built from UIowa-named files and holds none of them, so no pair is graded and no claim of resemblance is made

register control: read from the sound of each crescendo the site serves (the blowing pressure rising evenly from 3 Pa to 600 Pa over 6 s; 40 ms windows, each period by autocorrelation), the first register sounds from 103, 103, 78 and 99 Pa on F4, A4, Bb4 and B4. On F4 and A4 it holds to 444 and 480 Pa, then jumps to the pipe's second mode (743 and 884 Hz) for the rest of the ramp; on Bb4 and B4 it holds to the last window read, at 597 Pa. A real Bressan alto, measured on an artificial mouth, leaves its first register at F4 230, A4 305, Bb4 505 and B4 490 Pa: here the first register ends 1.93 and 1.57 times higher on F4 and A4, and on Bb4 and B4 lasts at least 1.18 and 1.22 times past the measured ceiling. Under the first register the pipe sounds higher modes: F4 its third (1166 Hz) at 58 to 87 Pa, A4 its third (1306 Hz) at 70 to 101 Pa and B4 a mode at 1231 to 1241 Hz from 66 to 97 Pa, 11.6 to 12.8 dB below the clip's loudest window (the median window at 60 to 100 Pa); A4 its second (912 Hz) at 34 to 64 Pa and Bb4 its second (958 Hz) at 40 to 68 Pa, 34 to 42 dB below. Under 30 Pa on A4 and Bb4, and under about 60 Pa on F4 and B4, the clips are 60 to 83 dB below their loudest window. The held F4 and A4 (135 and 210 Pa) sound the first mode, at 349.7 and 433.2 Hz. These reads are of the renders the site serves (the jet_transfer auvray-2014 row, no windway row, the contraction mouth loss); the register figures this entry printed before came from renders of 2026-10-31 that the site no longer serves. Diagnostic renders of the four crescendos (2026-11-08, one row changed at a time, not served) name the cause. With the mouth's contraction loss off (`mouth_loss none`) the first register sounds from 99, 99, 76 and 97 Pa to the top of the ramp on all four fingerings: the upper edge comes from the Auvray jet loop with no mouth nonlinearity, and only the contraction row, whose 0.9 is NOT A FIT, pulls F4 and A4 down to 444 and 480 Pa. With the convection ratio gamma 0.3 in place of 0.4 the first register starts 1.60, 1.79, 2.31 and 1.72 times higher (165, 185, 179 and 171 Pa; the jet delay alone scales by 1.78) and the higher modes under it move up with it: the lower-edge modes belong to the jet loop and move with gamma. The `jet_transfer nolle-price-2015 long-channel 0` row does not lock to the pipe on these cards: every fingering sounds near 400 Hz. A developing windway (the published 61.5 mm) cannot be combined with this card's Auvray jet row, which takes the exit speed U = sqrt(2P/rho) and refuses every windway law (flue_loop.rs:1637-1639, auvray_jet.rs:36-37); on the 600 Pa crescendos the slit's own developed-flow bound (Re_Dh 1760, bernoulli_aperture/developing.rs:208) refuses it first. The tin whistle's pages blow through other rows (a developing slit windway, the forced-Bickley jet response, contraction 0.6), so their registers are no evidence about these

the windway: its height is not published for this alto (only its length) and is estimated from two other instruments; its curved, crescent-shaped opening, the direction of its roof, the chamfers and the taper of its section are unknown, and the recipe has a straight rectangular slit. The pressure-to-jet-speed map and every register claim depend on the height, and a sweep of the published bounds has not been made

labium offset: DERIVED, not measured. The published step and edge give the edge underside 0.27 mm on the bore side of the jet centreline at the estimated windway height, and the jet splits at the middle of the 0.25 mm face: +0.1455 mm on the pipe side (face ends +0.02 to +0.27 mm; the windway-height bounds move it from -0.225 to +0.425 mm); jet angle zero. The served pages, every length 0.9067 of the Bressan's, carry it as +0.1319 mm, 0.34 of the Auvray row's Bickley half-width at the labium (2h/5 = 0.384 mm). That row splits the jet's flow as H b U (1 + tanh((eta - y_off)/b)) (auvray_jet.rs:10-12, flue_loop.rs:1780-1782), so the offset sets how much of the even harmonics the jet makes. Read on the clips the site serves (0.2 s Hann windows; the un-parity index of Auvray et al. 2015 is 10 log10 of the odd harmonics 3, 5 and 7 over the even 2, 4 and 6, in power): on the crescendos where the ramp passes 140 and 400 Pa, H2 sits below H1 by 30.5 and 25.6 dB on F4, 24.4 and 8.7 dB on A4, 21.6 and 17.6 dB on B-flat4, 32.6 and 33.4 dB on B4, and the index is -0.9 and -5.4 dB on F4, +13.5 and -20.1 dB on A4, +1.1 and -2.5 dB on B-flat4, -2.4 and +2.4 dB on B4; on the held F4 (135 Pa) and A4 (210 Pa), H2 is 30.8 and 19.1 dB below H1 and the index -0.6 and +6.0 dB. Auvray et al. 2015 measured about -2 dB at 140 and 400 Pa on a Zen-On Bressan head with a cylindrical foot (a comparison only: not this instrument). The jet's swing at the labium is not read on these renders
the second and third registers: the thumb hole is a fully open or closed hole; the half-closed thumb hole that raises the register is not modelled, so only first-register fingerings are rendered

pitch: hole 7's position is derived, not measured (bracket 18 to 30 mm); the finger holes have no undercutting, and the closed holes no matching volume or series length (the open holes carry their inner, matching and series lengths, which are open-hole forms); the labium edge height is inherited from the unknown windway height (an edge at the bore or 1.25 mm above it moves every note by about +10 or -9 cents, passive); the measured bore is the tabulated maximum of a shrunken, slightly oval boxwood joint (the head taken at the oval's area-equivalent diameter, the midpoint of its published 0.2 to 0.4 mm)

the jet: the `jet_transfer auvray-2014 0.3 0.4` row (Auvray, Fabre and Lagrée 2012; Auvray, Ernoult, Fabre and Lagrée 2014): receptivity in phase with the mouth's acoustic velocity at the flue exit, flat growth exp(beta W/h), pure convection at gamma U, a Bickley profile of half-width 2h/5 at the labium and Verge's distance (4/pi) sqrt(2hW) between the two injection points, with U = sqrt(2P/rho). It replaces the interim slot-jet card's band chain, convection ratio and demonstrator displacement gain of 90 (flue_loop.rs:1612-1617, 1775-1778, 1966-1969); of that card only the onset seed (1e-6 of the jet speed, flue_loop.rs:2163) still enters, and its Reynolds band is only reported block by block (flue_loop.rs:2403), not enforced. beta 0.3 and gamma 0.4 are the values Auvray et al. 2014 print in Table I, which hold over a few jet thicknesses and were validated on one Zen-On Bressan alto at W/h about 4; neither was measured on this instrument. On these cards W/h is 4.34, the growth to the labium 3.68, the half-width 0.384 mm and the injection distance 3.60 mm. The row takes its own exit speed and so refuses every windway law (auvray_jet.rs:36-37): no windway loss is in these pages
a spectrum and attack like a real recorder: the first register lasts far past the real instrument's ceiling (see register control), and no chiff or edge-tone noise is modelled

the gas beyond the breath law: the CO2 fraction is the published one for exhaled breath, not measured in a played recorder; no temperature gradient along the bore, and the published pitch was measured in rooms at 15 to 27 C (about 40 cents between them)
native verification beyond one fingering at two mechanics clocks and two jet seeds on a few files

Openings that hear each other: the open holes and the foot's open end radiate apart. Tried with every opening hearing every other free-field, after the travel time between them (`outlet_mutual free-field`), every page and scale or melody note with two or more holes open (the A4 held page; the A4, Bb4 and B4 crescendos; A4, Bb4, C5, D5, E5 and F5 in the stops) was refused before rendering, because with these loads the row is not passive: the real part of the openings' impedance matrix has a negative eigenvalue from the lowest frequencies up to 73 to 138 Hz with three openings, and up to 2.1 to 3.1 kHz with five to seven. The time step is not the cause: the exact free-field term with the loads' continuous form fails on the same notes. Each compact unflanged-pipe load's resistance falls short of a free-field monopole's by a share that grows with the square of frequency, and three or more openings in a line, closer together than a wavelength, radiate so nearly as one source that the matrix has less than that to spare. G4, with the foot and one hole open 78.2 mm apart, passes; it is not a page, so the row stays off the recorder

Openings that hear each other, weighted by their own radiation: tried with the free-field term between every pair of openings scaled by the square root of the two openings' own radiation resistances over a free-field monopole's (`outlet_mutual pritchard`; Pritchard 1960 as printed by Butler 2022, Eq. 1, with the geometric mean for unequal openings), which is passive with these loads by construction, every page and scale or melody note rendered. The row lowered the A4 held page, the A4, Bb4 and B4 crescendos by 0.7, 0.7, 0.4 and 0.2 c. A4 and B4 already sit flat of the recording, so the gap grew: 27.7 to 28.4 c on the A4 held page, 19.2 to 19.9 c on the A4 crescendo, 5.8 to 6.0 c on the B4 crescendo. Bb4 sits sharp and its gap shrank, 10.0 to 9.7 c, but the mean error of H2 to H12 against the recording grew, 15.07 to 15.27 dB. The mean error went 12.21 to 11.65 dB on the A4 held page, 9.936 to 9.941 dB on the A4 crescendo and 5.43 to 5.54 dB on the B4 crescendo. No page gains on both, so the row stays off. The half-space form of Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard (2013, Eq. 16), twice the free-field term, is set aside: with these unflanged loads it is not passive even for two openings

Separated flow at the openings: the flow leaving each open hole and the open end separates and loses its kinetic energy, a loss in series with each opening's own radiation (`opening_losses`, Δp = ρQ|Q|/(2(C_c A)²)). Tried with C_c 1 on every opening: the open end as Atig, Dalmont and Gilbert 2004 print it (C. R. Mécanique 332:299-304, Eq. 3, c_d = 2 for a thin-walled unflanged end), the side holes at the row's ceiling of 1, a loss 1.2 times the one Dalmont et al. 2002 print for a sharp-edged hole (Acta Acust. united Ac. 88:567-575, K_h = 0.5, as quoted by Szwarcberg et al. 2024, JASA, Sec. III.2.1, which is C_c 1.096): a C_c above 1 would be pressure recovery, which this row's full-head loss cannot represent. Every page rendered. The mean error of H2 to H12 against the recording grew on all six pages: 12.21 to 12.60 dB on the A4 held page, 9.61 to 9.81 dB on the F4 held page, and 9.94 to 12.34 dB, 15.07 to 16.67 dB, 5.43 to 12.12 dB and 11.94 to 12.44 dB on the A4, Bb4, B4 and F4 crescendos. The pitch moved by 0.5 c or less: the A4 held page went 0.5 c flatter, further from the recording; the A4 and B4 crescendos went 0.4 and 0.3 c sharper, closer to it; the Bb4 and F4 crescendos went 0.5 and 0.2 c sharper, further from it; the F4 held page moved less than 0.01 c. No page gains on both, so the row stays off

Room air on the way to the microphone (`observer_gas stokes-kirchhoff`, as the flute and whistle pages hear theirs), tried on all six pages on 2026-11-08: F4 crescendo plays it. On A4 held, F4 held, A4 crescendo, Bb4 crescendo and B4 crescendo it moved the mean error of H2 to H12 further from the recording, by 0.0016, 0.0023, 0.0013, 0.0009 and 0.0013 dB (from 12.2115 to 12.2131 dB on A4 held), and the pitch's distance from the recording by 0.000003 c or less, each below the precision these pages print (0.01 dB, 0.01 c). A page takes a row only if neither figure grows, so those five pages keep the live clip. The 17 stops of the scale and melody, tried with the same row on 2026-11-08 and read over each stop's steady part: the pitch's distance from equal temperament grows on 10 of them, by 0.000043 c at most (G4, 0.3 s), and on the 8 F4, A4 and Bb4 stops the mean error of H2 to H12 against that note's page recording grows on 5, by 0.0034 dB at most (A4, 0.9 s), each below the printed precision; the scale and melody take the row only if no stop's figure grows, so they keep the live stops
